nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?

Unknown if required evidence is insufficient or unresolved; do not infer completion, absence, or progress from unrelated edits.

Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is too broad: it asks only whether a mug is right of the headphones, so it treats the pre-existing right-side mug as fulfillment and ignores whether the requested move occurred. Bind the decision to the original and edited snapshots and assess progress of the same mug relative to the same headphones. Here, the source mug is left of the headphones; the edited image shows a mug on the right, but also retains a mug near the headphones and a blurred mug-shaped region at the original location. This supports some progress, not an unambiguous completed move. Preserve the rubric’s distinction between partial progress and completion, and use unknown only if the relevant objects or their correspondence cannot be resolved. The two support observations repeat the same endpoint claim and share a dependency, so they are not independent confirmation; require evidence that addresses change from the source rather than merely restating the final spatial relation. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported.
s2: The binding checks only the edited image’s endpoint, so it can pass because a mug is already to the headphones’ right, without establishing that the requested mug was moved. Make the support decision compare source and edited snapshots, track the same mug and headphones where correspondence is visually supportable, and report evidence of change as well as final position. In these images, the source mug is left of the headphones; the edit shows a mug on the right, another mug near the headphones, and a blurred mug-shaped region at the source location. This is evidence of some progress but does not clearly establish complete fulfillment; preserve the rubric’s partial-versus-complete distinction rather than treating any right-side mug as success. The dependent observations repeat the same endpoint claim, so they are not independent corroboration. Keep uncertainty for genuinely unresolved identity or position, not merely because the result is imperfect. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s1: The binding must preserve this node’s evidence-availability role: do not turn it into a fulfillment judgment or infer that a right-side mug proves the requested move. Compare the source and edited snapshots only as needed to identify the mug and headphones and determine whether their positions are observable; report visibility/identification evidence, not whether the edit is complete. The edited image contains multiple mug-like objects, including a blurred region at the source mug’s former location, so avoid silently treating any one mug as the original; express uncertainty if correspondence or position cannot be resolved. Keep the requested-change assessment to the fulfillment node, which should use source-to-edit change and the rubric’s partial-versus-complete distinction. The trace reports no transport, schema, or dependency failure; its high-confidence endpoint claim is not evidence that this support check should decide fulfillment.

The continuity check only distinguishes the original mug being to the right from certain cases where it was not moved toward the target; it leaves other non-complete placements unresolved, and no support check separately establishes whether the original mug moved closer to the right without reaching it. Thus the program can report unknown where the rubric requires partial for evidenced progress, or cannot distinguish no progress from progress in relevant cases. The broad visibility check and current-position check do not supply that missing evidence.

The fulfillment readout cannot reliably compose the evidence: `s2` is a support check whose criteria already assign complete/absent/partial/unknown, while `original_mug_progress` separately assesses source-anchored movement. The readout does not specify how to resolve conflicting observations from these checks. In particular, `s2` can pass because a mug is right of the headphones even when the source-anchored check fails, and its own criteria call that complete despite the readout correctly requiring the original mug. This overlapping completion rule risks unsupported completion. The source-anchored check otherwise appropriately distinguishes progress from a right-side mug alone.
